title: I know nothing about Indian philosophy
description: A gentle first walk through the big ideas that recur across Indian thought, anchored in the Bhagavad Gita. By the end you will know the core vocabulary and be ready to explore the individual schools.

steps.title: What is philosophy here?
steps.note: Indian schools are called darshanas, 'ways of seeing'. Each begins with how we know things (pramana) — a good first question.

steps.title: Philosophy begins with a real question
steps.note: The Gita opens with Arjuna confused about what is right and asking for guidance — philosophy as a response to a lived crisis.

steps.title: Dharma
steps.note: Order, duty, right conduct: the word that frames how one should act in the world.

steps.title: One's own duty
steps.note: The Gita's teaching that one's own path, imperfectly followed, is better than another's.

steps.title: Karma
steps.note: Action and its consequences — and the Gita's twist: the problem is attachment to results.

steps.title: Work without clinging to results
steps.note: The single most quoted teaching of the Gita.

steps.title: Who am I?
steps.note: Almost every school asks what the real self is; their answers divide them.

steps.title: The body changes, the experiencer continues
steps.note: A simple observation that launches the inquiry into the Self.

steps.title: Yoga
steps.note: Far more than posture: in the Gita and Patanjali, a discipline of mind and action.

steps.title: Moksha — liberation
steps.note: The highest aim for most schools, understood very differently by each.

steps.title: Bhakti — devotion
steps.note: The path of love for God, which shaped much of Indian religious life.

steps.title: A leaf, a flower, fruit or water
steps.note: Devotion needs nothing elaborate, only sincerity.

steps.title: Explore the schools: Vedanta
steps.note: The schools built on the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras and Gita.

steps.title: Sankhya
steps.note: A dualist map of consciousness and nature.

steps.title: The 25 principles
steps.note: Explore Sankhya's model of reality interactively.

steps.title: Buddhism
steps.note: A major tradition that denies a permanent self.

steps.title: Many-sided reality
steps.note: Try the Jain method of standpoints.
